title: bug: postflight-safe.mjs kills the wrapper harness at 60 min (:51), but at f38a17d4 the full postflight.ps1 takes 3200 s (5.1) and 3400 s (pwsh 7) on an idle Ryzen 9 9950X3D desktop, and windows-latest runs this work about 1.5x slower, so CI's "Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight" will end in failureClass TIMEOUT now that task-02af8654 lets the job reach it (the 30-min cap did the same on 10-31, a95f7199)
description:
Filed by hunt #25 (task-9ca91400, architect-67c762f6) on 2026-11-04. Lane: the windows-latest steps after step 15, which no completed PR #230 run had reached since 2037e856 (governor comment-f95ba6c8).

PROBLEM
- scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs runs postflight.sh or postflight.ps1 with execFile `timeout: 60 * 60 * 1000` and `killSignal: 'SIGKILL'` (:51-52).
  - A kill becomes failureClass TIMEOUT and exit 1 (:55, :8).
  - The comment at :45-48 sizes that bound on "about 20 minutes on a desktop and past 30 on windows-latest".
- The harness has grown since then. Between main (3ed7a299, the dependabot PR base) and f38a17d4:
  - postflight.ps1 went from 5013 to 6165 lines;
  - postflight-vm-route.ps1 went from 0 to 1008 lines;
  - the shared postflight-worktree.cjs gained 1340 lines;
  - postflight.sh went from 5645 to 6725 lines, and postflight-vm-route.sh from 0 to 777. 9e9e7345 (CQ-M07r) then added another 255 to postflight-vm-route.sh.
  - CQ-M07s and CQ-M07t (74fe4c99, 527735ea, open) add more VM-route scenarios to both suites.

EVIDENCE
1. Desktop run of the full harness at f38a17d4, using hunt #22's CI emulation (scripts in /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9ca91400/mine/: ci-lib.ps1, leg-p5.ps1, leg-p7.ps1, postflight-tee.mjs).
   - Emulation: env stripped, CI=true, a fresh HOME, an 8.3 TEMP, and the CI chain pwsh step -> node -> engine. postflight-tee.mjs repeats postflight-safe's exact execFile but keeps the output.
   - Deviation: GITHUB_ACTIONS was removed for that sub-step only. postflight.ps1:4317 is its only reader, the scenario AE symlink check this host cannot pass.
   - The host is an AMD Ryzen 9 9950X3D with 32 threads, at 13% CPU load sampled mid-run. The 5.1 and pwsh 7 runs overlapped.
   - Windows PowerShell 5.1: PASS in 3200 s, 89% of the cap. Verdict {"engine":"powershell","exit":0,"lastScenario":"Z","failureClass":"NONE"}. Log: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-9ca91400/logs/p5-postflight-ps1-full.log, last line "rawExit=0 failure=null secs=3200".
   - pwsh 7: PASS in 3400 s, 94% of the cap. Log: logs/p7-postflight-pwsh-full.log, "secs=3400".
2. Runner against desktop, for the same kind of work (sequential PowerShell and git process spawns):
   - Live CI run 41848822541 at 9e9e7345 on windows-latest:
     - "Test Windows PowerShell landing guard" took 47 s, against 30 s on this desktop (1.57x).
     - "Test PowerShell 7 landing guard" took 45 s, against 28 s (1.61x).
   - a95f7199 (10-31): run 41198897512's "Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight" was "killed at exactly 30:01", {"engine":"powershell","exit":1,"lastScenario":"Z","failureClass":"TIMEOUT"}, while the suite took about 20 min locally (1.5x or more).
   - Linux: postflight-safe bash took 1841 s in hunt #25's WSL run. ubuntu-latest's "Test Bash wrapper postflight and parity" took 2750 s at 80078651 (run 41834653023), 2692 s at 2037e856 and 2688 s at 060d7b8c. That is about 1.46x.
   - At 1.5x, 5.1 needs about 4800 s and pwsh 7 about 5100 s, against the 3600 s cap. To pass, the runner would have to be at most 12.5% slower than this desktop for 5.1, and 6% for pwsh 7.
3. Why CI has not shown it yet:
   - Since 2037e856 the windows-latest job stopped at step 15 (task-02af8654, DONE 9463e77d). Before that it stopped at the worktree suite (task-e45da220).
   - main-based runs (the dependabot PRs at 00:23Z) show main's smaller suite on windows-latest: 1846-2092 s for 5.1 and 1689-1948 s for pwsh 7.
4. Live: run 41848822541 (9e9e7345, which includes 02af8654's fix) passed windows-latest steps 15-20.
   - Step 22, "Test Windows PowerShell wrapper postflight", began at 15:14:00Z.
   - Predicted: it fails at about 16:18Z, after worktree-landing.ps1 and then the 60-min kill. Hunt #25 adds its outcome as a comment on this row.
5. ubuntu-latest already uses about 2690 s of the same cap (76%), before CQ-M07r's 255 new vm-route.sh lines.

FIX DIRECTION
- Raise the bound in postflight-safe.mjs so that the predicted runner time fits with headroom: at least 120 min.
  - ci.yml sets no timeout-minutes, so GitHub's 360-min job default still applies.
  - Keep SIGKILL and the TIMEOUT class.
  - Replace the :45-48 comment with the measured numbers above.
- Optional: an env override for the bound. It is not needed for the fix.
- Out of scope unless the governor asks: splitting the 5.1 and pwsh 7 postflights into separate jobs to cut wall time.
  - Two steps of about 80 min each make the Windows job about 3 h.
  - The concurrency group lets the run in progress finish, so PR #230 results would lag by that much.

FILES
- scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs
- scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs
- No open row holds either (lanes.js at 15:26Z).

NOTES FOR THE PLANNER
- epic-be924fb8 has no finalTaskId, so this newest row reads isEpicFinal:true through the max-order fallback. Keep the gate narrow: `node --test scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs`.
- Do not plan a full postflight run as the gate. It takes 55-60 min per engine on this desktop.

implementationPlan.description:
Test first, then the fix, in scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs and scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs only. Load test-driven-development. Read mem:task-task-5f7f43fa84ac448a853ac0cd625487c0-handoff. Write both files with your own editing tool (Claude Edit/Write, or apply_patch in a codex exec seat). Never use a shell write or `git apply`: a path written that way has no TOOL witness and is HELD at landing. The exact intended change (+36/-7, verified in planning) is at /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-5f7f43fa/intended.diff. Read it; do not apply it.

(1) TEST, RED first. In postflight-safe.test.mjs, change the import to `import { POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS, runPostflight, summarizePostflight } from './postflight-safe.mjs';`. Append one top-level async test, 'the harness bound is at least 120 minutes and a kill at the bound is a nonzero TIMEOUT':
(a) Three asserts on POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS: Number.isSafeInteger; `>= 120 * 60 * 1000` with the message `bound ${POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS} ms is under 120 min` (the gate greps 'is under 120 min'); and `< 360 * 60 * 1000` with the message `... reaches GitHub's 360-min job default` (a bound at or past the job default could never report TIMEOUT).
(b) For each engine of bash, powershell, pwsh: `const pass = `PASS postflight.${engine === 'bash' ? 'sh' : 'ps1'}``. Call `await runPostflight(engine, fake)`, where fake(file, args, options, callback) pushes {file, options} to a calls array, then calls `callback(Object.assign(new Error('Command failed'), { killed: true, code: null, signal: 'SIGKILL' }), `[scenario Q] ok\n${pass}\n`, '')`. That error is the shape Node's execFile gives a timeout kill. Assert calls.length 1, calls[0].file === engine, calls[0].options.timeout === POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS and calls[0].options.killSignal === 'SIGKILL'. deepEqual the result to { engine, exit: 1, lastScenario: 'Q', failureClass: 'TIMEOUT', failureLine: null }, so the PASS line cannot mask a kill.
(c) Then `await runPostflight(engine, (file, args, options, callback) => callback(null, `${pass}\n`, ''))` must deepEqual { engine, exit: 0, lastScenario: null, failureClass: 'NONE', failureLine: null }.
Run `node --test scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs` now. It must fail with `SyntaxError: The requested module './postflight-safe.mjs' does not provide an export named 'POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS'`. Quote that line in complete_step.

(2) FIX in postflight-safe.mjs.
(a) Right after the SKIP_LINE constant, add three lines: `// A harness run that outlives this bound is killed (SIGKILL) and reported as TIMEOUT.`, `// runPostflight's execFile comment gives the measured runs it is sized from.` and `export const POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS = 180 * 60 * 1000;`.
(b) `function runPostflight(engine) {` becomes `export function runPostflight(engine, run = execFile) {`, and `execFile(engine, args, {` becomes `run(engine, args, {`. The default keeps the CLI entry (:63-69, `runPostflight(process.argv[2])`) on the real execFile. A default parameter is the test seam because node:test cannot mock an ESM named import without an experimental flag that CI does not pass.
(c) `timeout: 60 * 60 * 1000,` becomes `timeout: POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS,`. Keep cwd, windowsHide, encoding, maxBuffer and killSignal 'SIGKILL' byte-identical.
(d) Keep the comment's first sentence and 'execFile keeps bounded buffers in memory and kills a timed-out/overlong child.'. Replace the rest (:46-48, from 'Windows PowerShell 5.1 runs every scenario' to 'so the bound is an hour.') so the block reads, in ASCII only (no x-sign, tilde-dash or em dash; the file is ASCII with LF):
`// Never inherit stdout/stderr or write them to artifacts. execFile keeps` / `// bounded buffers in memory and kills a timed-out/overlong child. Sizing,` / `// measured at f38a17d4 (task-5f7f43fa): the full postflight.ps1 took 3200 s` / `// under Windows PowerShell 5.1 and 3400 s under pwsh 7 on an idle desktop,` / `// and windows-latest runs this work about 1.5-1.6x slower (landing guards` / `// 47 s vs 30 s, 45 s vs 28 s), so 80-90 min there; ubuntu-latest's bash run` / `// took 2690-2750 s. 180 min keeps the slowest at about half the bound and` / `// well inside GitHub's 360-min job default.`
The bound is 180 min, not the DoD floor of 120: at 120 the predicted 85-91 min pwsh 7 runner step would sit at 71-76% of the cap, which is the ratio the governor (comment-7ed4d663) called too close on ubuntu-latest.

Error handling: the error mapping at :54-57 stays byte-identical, and so do summarizePostflight, ci.yml and every other file. The mapping order is: an ERR_CHILD_PROCESS_STDIO_MAXBUFFER code gives OUTPUT_LIMIT (checked before killed, because Node also kills on overflow); killed gives TIMEOUT; any other string code gives SPAWN_FAILED; a numeric code is the exit. The entry's catch still turns a thrown readFileSync or spawn error into SPAWN_FAILED. Re-run `node --test scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs`: 15 tests pass (the 14 existing plus 1 new).

executionContract.intendedBehavior: scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs kills a postflight harness run only after POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS = 180 min. The bound is exported (it was a private 60-min literal), and the kill still uses killSignal SIGKILL and still reports failureClass TIMEOUT with a nonzero exit. runPostflight is exported with an optional second parameter (default: node:child_process execFile), so a test can capture the real execFile options and drive the real error mapping without spawning a harness. The sizing comment at the execFile call cites measured runs instead of the old 20/30-minute estimate: 3200 s and 3400 s on the desktop at f38a17d4, windows-latest about 1.5-1.6x slower, and ubuntu-latest bash at 2690-2750 s.
acceptanceCriteria: `node --test scripts/tests/postflight-safe.test.mjs` passes 15 tests (the 14 existing plus 1 new) under WSL node and under Windows node.exe.

The new test fails if POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS is under 120 min, 0, not a safe integer, or 360 min or more. It also fails if the execFile call stops passing POSTFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS or SIGKILL, or if a killed child stops mapping to failureClass TIMEOUT with exit 1. The step-3 mutants show each of these.
The gate's 119-min mutant fails on the 'is under 120 min' assertion, not on a syntax or import error.
The sentence 'about 20 minutes on a desktop and past 30 on windows-latest' is gone. The comment names 3200 s, 3400 s and the 1.5-1.6x runner ratio, and both files stay ASCII.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:
- A bound of exactly 120 min (the DoD floor). The predicted pwsh 7 runner step (85-91 min) would sit at 71-76% of the cap, the same ratio the governor already called too close on ubuntu-latest (comment-7ed4d663), and CQ-M07s and CQ-M07t are adding scenarios now. At 180 min the slowest step sits near 50%. A failed step skips the rest of the job, so a real hang costs about 14 + 180 min on windows-latest, roughly the length of a normal passing Windows job (two postflight steps of about 85 min each).
- An env override, optional in the task: skipped. Changing a constant is the same one-line review as changing ci.yml.
- Per-engine budgets: more code for no gain. One bound sized for the slowest engine leaves bash at about 26%.
- Splitting the Windows postflights into separate jobs: out of scope unless the governor asks.
- Grepping the source text for the bound: brittle, and it would not prove the execFile call uses the bound. The default-parameter seam on runPostflight proves the real options and the real kill mapping instead.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights:
- postflight-safe.mjs is the only bound on the three CI postflight steps: ci.yml has no timeout-minutes, and GitHub's job default is 360 min.
- summarizePostflight maps failure 'TIMEOUT' to exit 1 even when a PASS line is present.
